xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3410: design(dashboard): style guide v2 — Geist type system, display scale, chips, soft cards, page-not-modal doctrine

plan.title: design(dashboard): style guide v2 — Geist type system, display scale, chips, soft cards, page-not-modal doctrine
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: The current style guide caps ALL type at font-medium and defines no display tier, so no dashboard surface can read as a page — everything reads as a panel, and creation flows land as cramped dialogs because the system has no vocabulary for anything bigger. Separately, all fonts load from the Google Fonts CDN.
narratives.Proposal: Ship the v2 vocabulary as a selectable appearance theme, not a cutover: 'Overdeck Theme' (ui.theme in ~/.overdeck/config.yaml + a two-card picker in Settings → Appearance) chooses between Ledger (current style, frozen legacy) and Broadsheet (new default: Geist/Geist Mono variable typefaces, tiered weights, display scale, hero placeholders, eyebrow labels, chips, soft cards, keycap CTAs, dot-metadata lines). A single data-theme attribute on the document root carries the theme; Broadsheet-only utilities resolve to Ledger-safe fallbacks so v2-vocabulary surfaces degrade but never break under Ledger. All four font families self-host; the Google Fonts links are removed. The page-not-modal doctrine lands as a named guide rule (PAN-3411 is its first consumer). Color discipline, semantic tokens, and the badge tint formula stay identical in both themes.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Color palette changes
- Component-by-component restyling to the new patterns (per-feature adoption; PAN-3411 first)
- Dark-mode rework — the dark/light subsystem (useTheme, ui-theme.json, .dark class) is untouched except naming disambiguation
- Per-user or per-project themes (the setting is per-instance)
- Additional themes beyond Ledger and Broadsheet
- Any backend change beyond the ui.theme config schema key and its settings-API surfacing
- Migrating NewProjectModal to a page (follow-up issue only, folded into item user-docs-appearance)

autoDecisions.summary: Keep the PRD's ui.theme YAML key but name ALL new code identifiers 'DesignLanguage' (type DesignLanguage, useDesignLanguage(), localStorage overdeck.ui.designLanguage); rewrite the stale schema.ts:429 comment.
autoDecisions.rationale: The dark/light subsystem already owns UiTheme/useTheme/overdeck.ui.theme/ui-theme.json/PUT /api/settings/ui-theme; the PRD is authoritative on the YAML surface, so the collision is resolved at the code-identifier layer.

autoDecisions.summary: Boot-before-paint mirrors the dark/light flash-prevention pattern: inline index.html script sets data-theme from a localStorage mirror (default broadsheet); useDesignLanguage reconciles from GET /api/settings on mount.
autoDecisions.rationale: Satisfies NFR-4 (instant switch, no boot flash) without blocking first paint on a network fetch, reusing a proven in-repo pattern (index.html:12-21, useTheme.ts).

autoDecisions.summary: Fonts live in src/dashboard/frontend/public/fonts/; the Geist pair is copied from the committed design/style-guide/mockups/fonts/; DM Sans + Space Grotesk variable woff2 come from an OFL source at implementation time.
autoDecisions.rationale: public/ is the existing Vite static-asset path; the Geist files are already reviewed and committed at ~57KB each, well inside the 500KB NFR budget.

autoDecisions.summary: Broadsheet --font-mono = 'Geist Mono Variable' with the SF Mono stack as in-stack fallback; identifiers and eyebrows both consume var(--font-mono).
autoDecisions.rationale: Directly implements PRD D-1 ('mono is Geist Mono Variable' + 'SF Mono stack remains the terminal/code fallback') and D-5 (eyebrow is Geist Mono) without a second mono token.

autoDecisions.summary: User-facing docs = new configuration/appearance.mdx plus a docs.json nav entry.
autoDecisions.rationale: No appearance/settings doc exists today (verified: configuration/ has 14 pages, none for appearance); a new page is the smallest additive change.

autoDecisions.summary: Badge radius rounded-sm→rounded-md applies only under [data-theme="broadsheet"]; Ledger badges stay rounded-sm.
autoDecisions.rationale: PRD D-11 sanctions exactly one texture change; scoping it to Broadsheet preserves the Ledger pixel-parity regression bar (D-12).

autoDecisions.summary: 'Pixel-parity' for Ledger is defined as computed-style + layout/box parity, not glyph rasterization parity.
autoDecisions.rationale: Google serves unicode-range-subsetted woff2; self-hosting DM Sans makes byte-identical rasterization unachievable by construction, so layout parity is the only honest bar (recorded as PRD D-22).

narrative.Action: In src/dashboard/frontend/src/index.css define --font-sans, --font-display, and --font-mono CSS variables: :root carries today's exact Ledger values (--font-sans: "DM Sans", system-ui, sans-serif; --font-display: "Space Grotesk", system-ui, sans-serif; --font-mono: the current SF Mono-first stack), and [data-theme="broadsheet"] overrides them (--font-sans: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; --font-display: "Geist Variable", system-ui, sans-serif; --font-mono: "Geist Mono Variable", "SF Mono", "SFMono-Regular", Consolas, "Liberation Mono", monospace). Repoint the three fontFamily entries in src/dashboard/frontend/tailwind.config.js:67-71 at the variables. Add the named Broadsheet utilities as CSS component classes (port the values from the working prototype at design/style-guide/mockups/style-guide-v2.html lines 44-66 and 252-253 — do not reinvent): .display-xl (clamp(48px, 7vw, 72px), tracking-tight, font-weight 700-800), .display-lg (~40px, weight 650-700), .eyebrow (var(--font-mono), 11px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.12em, text-muted-foreground). Under [data-theme="ledger"] (and by default at :root) the same utilities resolve to the Ledger-safe fallbacks: display-xl → text-xl font-medium, display-lg → text-lg font-medium, eyebrow → text-xs uppercase tracking-wider font-medium. Intermediate weights (480, 650) are set via CSS font-weight on the named utility only — never ad-hoc font-[480] classes. No !important, no hex.

metadata.sizeJustification: The issue body defines this as one deliverable set: theme plumbing, fonts, the law-file and skill rewrites, and the bounded migration are a single feature — a selectable theme shipped without its config key, picker, fonts, or law-file update is not usable, and the slices are not independently shippable (fonts without tokens are dead assets; a config key without the picker is unreachable; docs without the feature describe nothing). The 8 subsystems (src/dashboard frontend, src/lib config+settings-api, tests, design law, bundled skill, user docs) are the irreducible span of that one feature, not separable workstreams.
